questions.text: I tend to notice my emotional reactions in retrospect rather than being gripped by them in the moment.
I would rather be an integral part of a large group than lead a small one.
I detect the emotional residue in a room where something intense just happened.
I maintain an orderly queue of tasks rather than juggling them all at once.
I seldom find myself concerned about how another person's difficulties will turn out.
I find that working behind the scenes for others' benefit is more satisfying than being in the spotlight.
I treat my calendar as a rough suggestion that I adjust throughout the day.
I do not pick up on the nonverbal signals that indicate whether a group wants my input.
Someone's suffering matters to me even when they can't put their need into words.
I prefer to be the one who communicates bad news to the team.
I notice that my jaw clenches and my shoulders tense the instant I feel threatened or upset.
Others' pain rarely feels like it matters to me, even when I know them well.
I notice that I can re-enter a stressful situation after a break without the stress having compounded.
I notice that my pulse and breathing remain steady even during emotionally charged discussions.
I frequently take on the role of gatekeeper for quality in group work.
I feel that enjoying the fruits of my own labor is exactly what hard work is for.
Being close to someone's suffering rarely makes it matter more to me.
I devote a fixed portion of my income to savings regardless of circumstances.
I frequently take on supporting or facilitating roles in team settings.
When I'm in the grip of a strong emotion, the world outside of it seems to temporarily cease to exist.
Someone's suffering stays on my mind until I know they are all right.
I find deep contentment in giving away things I worked hard to earn.
I tend to miss when a conversational pause is an invitation for me to share something personal.
I pick up on the subtle cues that indicate someone feels out of place in a group.
When I feel gratitude, it swells inside me until I can barely contain it.
I feel responsible for keeping a group on track toward its goals.
I feel comfortable dropping a project when my interest shifts to something more compelling.
I do not naturally notice the way people position themselves during a photo to signal closeness or distance.
I would sacrifice a personal milestone to attend to someone else's urgent need.
I find that maintaining a wish list of things I want for myself keeps me motivated.
I often feel drawn to check in on people I know are having a hard time, even when they haven't asked.
I tend to define success in terms of my own benchmarks, not in terms of what I did for others.
I notice that I calibrate my effort to match the group's established rhythm.
I pay bills and handle obligations when I notice them rather than setting up automation.
I pick up on when someone shortens their responses as a signal they want the conversation to end.
I maintain version histories of important documents so I can revert changes if needed.
